title: Finland – Cleaning services – Prosessisiivous Naantalin voimalaitoksella
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat Turun Seudun Energiantuotanto Oy:n (TSE) omistaman Naantalin tuotantoyksikön sekä niiden yhteisten prosessijärjestelmien teollisuussiivouspalvelut. Siivousalueeseen kuuluvat kaikki voimalaitosalueen tuotantotilat, mukaan lukien voimalaitosyksiköt 1–4, varaosavarastot, koneistamo, vesilaitos, kaukolämpöpumppaamo sekä polttoainekuljetinjärjestelmät. Työn luonne ja turvallisuusvaatimukset Voimalaitosympäristössä suoritettava siivoustyö on fyysisesti vaativaa johtuen muun muassa korkeista lämpötiloista, epäpuhtauksista ja ahtaista työskentelytiloista. Työturvallisuus on keskeinen osa palvelun toteuttamista. Työskentely voimalaitosalueella tulee suorittaa laitoksen kulloinkin voimassa olevien turvallisuusohjeiden mukaisesti. Erityistä turvallisuutta edellyttävissä työtehtävissä, kuten säiliötöissä ja putoamisvaarallisissa töissä, on noudatettava kyseisiä työtehtäviä koskevia turvallisuusmääräyksiä ja -menettelyjä. Työn yhteydessä syntyvät jätteet tulee lajitella voimassa olevien jätehuolto-ohjeiden mukaisesti. Toimittajalla tulee olla käytössään työn suorittamiseen riittävä ja tarkoituksenmukainen siivouskalusto. Henkilöstö ja työmäärä Kokemusperäisen arvion mukaan palvelun toteuttamiseen tarvitaan keskimäärin neljä (4) henkilöä marras-maaliskuun aikana ja kolme (3) henkilöä huhti-lokakuun aikana. Työmäärä on yhteensä arviolta noin 6 500 työtuntia vuodessa. Työryhmään tulee kuulua vähintään yksi kärkimiehenä toimiva, työhön osallistuva työnjohtaja. Henkilöstötarve voi vaihdella voimalaitosten käyttötavan, kuormitustilanteen sekä käytettävien polttoaineiden perusteella. Arvioidusta henkilöstömäärästä poikkeamisesta sovitaan aina tapauskohtaisesti etukäteen tilaajan kanssa. Työn organisointi Toimittajan henkilöstö työskentelee tilaajan työnjohdon ohjauksessa. Tilaaja määrittää suoritettavat siivoustehtävät, suunnittelee työkokonaisuudet sekä myöntää työtehtävien suorittamisen edellyttämät työluvat. Henkilöstön saatavuus Toimittajan henkilöstön saatavuuden vasteaika on enintään kahdeksan (8) tuntia tilauksesta työpäivisin klo 7.00–17.00. Muina aikoina vasteaika on enintään 24 tuntia tilauksesta. Vasteaika koskee yhden työparin toimittamista tilaajan käyttöön. Tilaajalla on oikeus muuttaa työvoimatarvetta, työjakson aloitusajankohtaa sekä työjakson kestoa ilmoittamalla muutoksesta toimittajalle vähintään 24 tuntia etukäteen. Muutosten perusteena voivat olla esimerkiksi muutokset laitoksen käyttötilanteessa, työsuunnitelmissa tai työaikatauluissa. Toimittaja vastaa kaikista sellaisista välittömistä kustannuksista, jotka aiheutuvat toimittajan työkomennuksen aikana tekemistä henkilöstömuutoksista. Vastuut ja velvoitteet Toimittaja vastaa aiheuttamistaan vahingoista tilaajan koneille, laitteille, työvälineille sekä käyttöönsä saamilleen työkaluille voimassa olevan vahingonkorvauslainsäädännön ja sopimusehtojen mukaisesti. Toimittaja vastaa käyttämiensä aliurakoitsijoiden työstä, toiminnasta ja toimituksista kuten omastaan. Toimittaja vastaa siitä, että Turun Seudun Energiantuotanto Oy:n työturvallisuusohjeet, turvallisuuskäytännöt ja työmaakohtaiset määräykset saatetaan sen oman henkilöstön sekä mahdollisten aliurakoitsijoiden tietoon ja että niitä noudatetaan kaikessa työskentelyssä. Dokumentaatio ja raportointi Tilaaja luovuttaa toimittajan käyttöön työn suorittamisen kannalta tarvittavan dokumentaation. Toimittajan tulee palauttaa kaikki tilaajan luovuttamat asiakirjat ja aineistot tilaajan edustajalle työn valmistuttua, ellei toisin sovita. Toimittajan tulee raportoida kirjallisesti kaikki suoritetut toimenpiteet, tehdyt havainnot sekä työn aikana havaitut poikkeamat. Raportti on toimitettava tilaajan edustajalle viipymättä työn valmistumisen jälkeen. Tilaajan järjestämät resurssit Tilaaja luovuttaa toimittajan henkilöstön käyttöön veloituksetta työn suorittamisessa tarvittavat erikoistyökalut, työhön kuuluvat materiaalit sekä käytettävissä olevat sosiaalitilat. Tarjouspyynnön liitteissä on tarkempaa tietoa hankinnan sisällöstä. Tarjoajan tulee huomioida liiteaineisto tarjouksen valmistelussa. Pakollinen tutustuminen työskentely-ympäristöön Tarjoajan edellytetään osallistuvan hankintayksikön järjestämään voimalaitosalueen esittelyyn ennen tarjouksen jättämistä, jotta tarjoajalle selviää työskentely-ympäristö ja vallitsevat olosuhteet. Esittelyn ajankohdat ja toteutus on kuvattu tämän tarjouspyynnön kohdassa "Muut ehdot". Sopimuskausi Molempia osapuolia sitova sopimuskausi on 24 kuukautta ajalla 1.4.2027–31.3.2029. Tämän jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana, ellei jompikumpi sopimusosapuoli irtisano sopimusta. Sopimuksen irtisanomisaika toistaiseksi voimassaolevalla sopimuskaudella on tilaajan osalta kuusi (6) kuukautta ja toimittajan osalta kaksitoista (12) kuukautta.

title: Finland – Computer equipment and supplies – Tienvarsiteknologian kapasiteettilaitteistot ohjelmistoineen
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat Fintraffic Tie Oy:n (jäljempänä myös "Hankintayksikkö" ja "Tilaaja") nykyisen tienvarsiteknologian kapasiteettipalvelun (jäljempänä myös "TVT-KaPa") korvaava kapasiteettilaitteistot tarvittavine ohjelmistoineen. Hankinnan kohde ja sen vaatimukset on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyyntöaineistossa. Toimituksen tavoitteena on rakentaa Tilaajalle uusi, tuotantokelpoinen, turvallinen, vikasietoinen ja hallitusti ylläpidettävä konesaliympäristö sekä siirtää sovitut nykyiset palvelut ja työkuormat uuteen ympäristöön. Toimituksen lopputuloksena Tilaajalla tulee olla käyttövalmis konesali- ja virtualisointiympäristö, keskitetysti hallittava verkko- ja tietoturvaratkaisu, hallittu virtuaalikoneiden ajopalvelu, hallittu kontti- ja Kubernetes-palvelu, hallittu tietokantapalvelu, hallittu kuormantasauspalvelu, hallittu varmistus- ja palautumisratkaisu, keskitetty valvonta ja lokitus, automatisoitava ja versionhallittu konfiguraationhallinta sekä dokumentoidut ylläpito-, muutos-, häiriö- ja palautumismenettelyt. Toimittaja vastaa siitä, että toimitetut osakokonaisuudet muodostavat yhteentoimivan kokonaisuuden ja ovat valmiita tuotantokäyttöön. Hankittavien laitteiden ja ohjelmistojen lisäksi hankintaan kuuluu tarvittavat käyttöönotto- ja migraatiopalvelut, korjaus-, asennus-, asiantuntija- ja jatkokehityspalvelut sekä ohjelmistopäivitykset (tarvittaessa) ja VMware Virtual Cloud Foundation 9 (VCF9) -teknologian myötä tulleiden uusien ominaisuuksien lanseeraamisen nykyisestä alustasta hankittavaan ratkaisuun. Hankittavien laitteiden tulee sisältää viiden (5) vuoden 24/7 ylläpito laitteistojen toimittajan taholta. Tilaaja hankkii kapasiteettilaitteistot liikenteenhallinnan työkuormien ajoon. Hankinnalla tavoitellaan maksimaalista käytettävyysastetta, selkeää ja toimintavarmaa arkkitehtuuria perus- ja poikkeustilanteissa. Ratkaisun tulee perustua Hyperkonvergenssilaitteisiin (jäljempänä HCI), VMware-virtuaalikoneiden virtualisaatioalustapalveluun (VSAN ready klusteri) ja varmistusratkaisuun sekä NAS-levyjärjestelmään. Nykyinen kapasiteettiratkaisu perustuu VMware vSphere virtualisointiteknologiaan, erillisellä NAS levyjärjestelmällä ja tallennusratkaisulla. Kapasiteettialustan virtualisointiteknologia päivittyy hankinnan myötä hyödyntämään VMware Virtual Cloud Foundation 9 teknologiaa. Tilaaja jatkaa VMware teknologian käyttöä ja on erikseen hankkinut tarvittavat lisenssit VMware alustalle. TVT-KaPa:n automatisoidusta valvonnasta, operoinnista ja vikatilanteisiin liittyvästä työnohjauksesta vastaa Tilaajan hallinta- ja valvontapalveluja toimittava, ns. ”HALVAL-toimittaja”. Lisäksi HALVAL-toimittaja vastaa jo olemassa olevista fyysisistä konesaliverkoista sekä Tilaajan runkoverkosta. Hankintayksikkö valitsee kilpailutuksen perusteella kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimman tarjouksen tehneen tarjoajan, jolta tilaukset tehdään. Kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimpana pidetään tarjousta, joka on hinnaltaan halvin. Hankittaville palveluille asetetut laadulliset vaatimukset ja näkökulmat on otettu huomioon vähimmäisvaatimuksissa. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin. LISÄHANKINTAMAHDOLLISUUDET (OPTIO) VARMUUSKOPIOINTILAITTEISTO Hankintaan sisältyy optiona kapasiteettilaitteiston varmuuskopiointilaitteisto (backup) ohjelmistoineen. Varmuuskopiointilaitteiston vaatimusmäärittely on hankintailmoituksen julkaisuhetkellä vielä kesken, mutta aikataulullisista syistä Hankintayksikkö ei voi enää lykätä kilpailutusta. Vaatimusmäärittelyä ei ole mahdollista tehdä loppuun ennen hankintailmoituksen julkaisua. Varmuuskopiointilaitteiston vaatimusmäärittely tullaan tekemään sopimuskauden aikana. Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden optiona hankkia varmuuskopiointilaitteiston sopimustoimittajaksi valitulta tarjoajalta. Hankintayksikkö ei kuitenkaan ole velvollinen hankkimaan laitteistoa sopimustoimittajalta, vaan Hankintayksikkö voi harkintansa mukaan hankkia varmuuskopiointilaitteiston myös muulla tavalla, esimerkiksi kilpailuttamalla. Optiona hankittavan varmuuskopiointilaitteiston arvo voi olla enintään 500 000 euroa (alv 0 %). MUUT LISÄHANKINTAMAHDOLLISUUDET Hankintaan sisältyy optiona laitejärjestelmien muutos- ja laajennusmahdollisuudet, jotka on kuvattu liitteessä B.4 Hinnat. Lisäksi Hankintayksikkö voi hankkia tarpeen vaatiessa sopimuskauden aikana muita sellaisia laitteita ja ohjelmistoja, jotka se kokee tarpeelliseksi esimerkiksi jatkokehityksen kannalta, ja jotka eivät muodosta merkittävää osaa sopimuksen arvosta. Optioiden mahdollinen käyttöönotto on hankintayksikön oikeus, ei velvollisuus.

title: Refuse Collection
description: NAICS Code: 562111, Solid Waste Collection PSC Code: S205, Housekeeping�Trash/Garbage Collection Place of Performance: Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico The Mission and Installation Contracting Command, MICC-Fort Buchanan is conducting market research to identify capable small and other business concerns that can provide non-personal solid waste management services for U.S. Army Garrison Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico. This Sources Sought notice is for planning and market-research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The anticipated requirement includes the collection, transportation, diversion, and disposal of non-hazardous municipal solid waste generated by commercial, industrial, housing, and community-activity areas on the installation. The contractor would be responsible for furnishing the personnel, supervision, vehicles, equipment, containers, and other resources necessary to perform scheduled and unscheduled refuse services. Waste must be transported and disposed of in accordance with applicable Federal, Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and local requirements, including disposal at an appropriately permitted Subtitle D municipal solid waste landfill in Puerto Rico. The contractor would be responsible for applicable disposal and tipping fees. Anticipated services include, but are not limited to: Collection of refuse from dumpsters, compactors, roll-off containers, and other approved collection containers; Collection frequency sufficient to prevent unsanitary conditions, with a general minimum service frequency of once per week and adjusted frequencies for waste streams or demand conditions as required; Collection of food waste, general refuse, green/yard waste, bulk waste, and other non-hazardous solid-waste streams identified in the final requirement; Maintenance, repair, replacement, relocation, cleaning, and sanitization of collection containers, as applicable; Removal of litter and waste within the designated area surrounding collection points, cleanup of spills caused by collection operations, and correction of contractor-caused unsanitary conditions; Development and execution of Government-approved collection routes, annual schedules, and weekly work schedules; Provision of additional containers, additional collection runs, and container relocations for special events, unit moves, organizational activities, small projects, and other surge requirements; Support during storms, natural disasters, installation closures, and emergency conditions, including rapid response capability for life, health, or safety emergencies; and Collection of service data and submission of required reports, including container weights, collection frequency, landfill tonnage, diversion or recycling data as applicable, container-condition reports, and work-control records. The contractor must be capable of maintaining service continuity during vehicle breakdowns and periods of increased demand. Collection vehicles and equipment must be safe, properly maintained, and suitable for municipal solid-waste collection operations. The contractor may not accept or dispose of hazardous waste, regulated medical waste, ammunition, explosives, firearms, asbestos, or other prohibited materials; such items must be reported in accordance with Government direction. title: Forbruksartikler til renhold og kantinedrift
description: Bakgrunn og formål Vestfold fylkeskommune har i dag en rammeavtale for kjøp av renholds-, papir-, plast- og storkjøkkenprodukter. Avtalen har sluttdato i januar 2027, og det er derfor behov for å gjennomføre en ny anskaffelse for å etablere en ny rammeavtale fra samme tidspunkt. Anskaffelsen skal dekke fylkeskommunens løpende behov for varer og tilhørende tjenester til renhold og kantinedrift ved videregående skoler, tannklinikker, museer og fylkeshuset. Formålet er å sikre stabil forsyning, effektiv drift og lik kvalitet over tid på tvers av lokasjoner. Det er samtidig et mål at den nye rammeavtalen legger til rette for et hensiktsmessig standardsortiment med nødvendige lokale tilpasninger, god sortimentsstyring og en brukervennlig bestillingsløsning. Fylkeskommunen ønsker også produkter og emballasjeløsninger med bedre miljøegenskaper, samt sikker kompatibilitet mellom forbruksartikler, dispensere og maskiner. Produktgrupper det er behov for er: Avfallshåndtering Hygieneprodukter Kantineprodukter Renoldsmidler Renholdsprodukter Tørkepapir

title: 6515--FY27 Cystos, Scopes and Resectoscope Trays
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 8, hereby provides notice of its intent to award a sole-source, fixed, contract to OLYMPUS AMERICA INC for its Olympus Cystos, Scopes and Resectoscope Trays. The contract is expected to be awarded IAW FAR 13.106-1(1), soliciting from a single source, the VA has determined this BRAND NAME ONLY requirement is limited to only one responsible source that can provide the supplies or services at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized. The requirement is for brand name only requested instruments must be manufactured by Olympus to ensure compatibility with the existing Olympus surgical visualization systems equipment currently deployed within the Orlando VA Healthcare System Operating Room suites. The existing inventory assigned to equipment inventory list 43ELN includes Olympus Hopkins 0° and 30° telescopes, Olympus IMAGE 1 HD camera heads, Olympus UltraMini HDi surgical systems, and Olympus TwinBeam HDi systems. These assets are presently in clinical service and utilized for endoscopic and minimally invasive surgical procedures. The Contractor shall provide all labor, tools, materials, supervision, and transportation necessary to complete installation and turnover to the Government. The contract will be a firm fixed price contract with the NAICS Code of 339112 with a small business size standard of $1 Million. A Sole Source Justification has been prepared. The delivery requirement is requested 90 days ARO. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. It is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available. A determination not to compete is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any response showing interest in this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be in the best interest of the Government. Responsible sources interested may submit a capabilities statement that proves by the preponderance of the evidence that another contractor can provide the specific products requested for Orlando VA Veterans Hospital. Responses must be received no later than 10:00am EST on November 27, 2026. No telephone inquiries or emails with questions will be accepted. Responses may be emailed to Susan.Rodriguez-Perez@va.gov.

title: Fabrication of a Replacement Stilling Well Platform and Associated Components for the Pointe-des-Cascades Hydrometric Station (02MC005), Fleuve Saint-Laurent, Québec
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) is seeking a fixed price quote for construction services to complete the fabrication of a steel platform for a new stilling well installation at the hydrometric station identified as 02MC005 Saint Laurent (Fleuve) à Pointe-des-Cascades located in Pointe-des-Cascades near Montréal, Québec. The installation and decommissioning components of the project have been included as optional deliverables. This project work is associated with a life cycle replacement of the stilling well which is no longer functioning due to rust out. The new stilling well will improve the accuracy of water level monitoring on the St. Lawrence River and allow for safe and efficient operation of the hydrometric station. The objective of this project is for the Contractor to fabricate a hot-dip galvanized steel grated platform and associated components in accordance with the drawing package provided in Appendix B. The installation of the platform, stilling well, and other project components (listed below) are optional work, which may only be exercised through a contract amendment before the expiry of the contract. The requirement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. Responses to this notice will determine the feasibility and/or basis for the Navy�s decision to proceed with an acquisition. Information received in relation to this notice will be used to assist the Government in developing an overall acquisition strategy, including the type and number of contracts and use of small business concerns. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this synopsis. Large business submittals will not be considered. NAVFAC Atlantic is seeking to identify potential sources with the capacity, experience and interest in competing for a contract for a Single Award Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-engineering (A/E) Contract for Environmental Planning and Engineering Services of an interdisciplinary nature for the implementation of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Executive Order (EO) 12114, Environmental Effects Abroad of Major Federal Actions �Ship Homeporting and Related Operational Issues. The principal geographic area covered by this contract encompasses NAVFAC Atlantic's AOR, NAVFAC Pacific�s AOR and the adjacent waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, including the Continental United States, the Caribbean, Europe, and North Africa. Additionally, tasks associated with this contract may be assigned anywhere in the world. The NAICS code for this proposed procurement is 541330 (small business size standard is $25.5 million). If the solicitation is issued, the solicitation will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year options totaling five (5) years of performance. The anticipated total work to be issued over the life of the contract via task orders (base year plus four one-year options) shall not exceed the estimated maximum amount of $75 million. The successful contractor to any forthcoming solicitation shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, and all equipment necessary to perform the services listed below. The preponderance of the work under this contract shall involve the accomplishment of work in the following major categories, including but not limited to: The general scope of this contract requires engineering services, biological science, physical science, cultural resource, community planning, and military operations specialists. The engineers and community planners providing services under this contract must have competence attested by a licensor as a professional engineer or certified planner. title: NCSS - Sentec tCOM+ Transcutaneous CO2 Monitor Acq
description: (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. (ii) The solicitation number is 75N98027Q00094. This solicitation is issued as a Notice of Intent (NOI) for a non-competitive combined synopsis/solicitation to award a contract or purchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name, if applicable). This acquisition is conducted under the authority of FAR 12.603, Streamlined Solicitation for Commercial Products or Commercial Services, and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Additional authority includes 41 U.S.C. 1901 and FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii). The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director, Office of Acquisitions, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a non-competitive basis to Sentec Inc., 40 Albion Road, Suite 100, Lincoln, RI 02865 for the acquisition of a Sentec tCOM+ transcutaneous CO2 (tcPCO2) monitor with V-sign Sensor 2, including on-site installation, support, and clinical education. The tCOM+ transcutaneous CO2 monitor meets the critical diagnostic need for accurate data collection, precise quality control procedures, and safe probe temperature regulation during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Furthermore, this specific monitor is currently utilized in other areas of the NIH Clinical Center, such as the Sleep Lab, and is required to maintain clinical standardization, sensor/consumable interoperability, and longitudinal data continuity throughout diagnostic testing across ongoing NHLBI research protocols. Sentec Inc. is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and sole distributor of the required system. (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective March 13, 2026 (03/13/2026). (iv) The associated NAICS code is 334510 (Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing), and the small business size standard is 1,250 employees. This requirement is not set aside for small business.

title: Intent to Sole Source - Type-C A&E Services for Construction of SFS Facility
description: The 145th Mission Support Group Contracting office in Charlotte, NC intends to issue a written request for proposal and resulting firm-fixed price sole source award to AECOM. This sole source award will be for Type �C� services for construction contract administration for the Construction of the Security Forces Building project. Type �C� services include but are not limited to documenting and providing answers to contractor�s requests for information, submittal reviews, attendance and records at progress meetings, review of lab results, preparation of as-built drawings, and multiple site visits to inspect the building during construction. This requirement is a follow-on award to AECOM. The requirement was previously negotiated and awarded via task order W50S87-21-F-5013. That award included Type A and B services for the design of the Construction of the Security Forces Building project. Type A services included the basis of design (specifically the design intent), the development of the project concept, and associated site investigations. The Type B services included the design narrative and the development of the construction documents. Because AECOM designed and certified the drawings and specifications and is liable for the quality of their design, it is economical and efficient to award the Type C services as a sole source follow-on contract. There is tremendous performance and liability risk associated with another A-E firm taking over the Type C services for a project that was designed by a different firm. Having the original designer, AECOM, on contract to perform the construction phase services is necessary for the Government to ensure responsibility for their design, including ensuring the design is constructible, maintainable and operable, that the project documentation is clear, sufficiently detailed, accurate and coordinated, and contains minimal errors. An award to a new A-E other than AECOM would increase the risk associated with these issues and potentially affect the Government�s rights under FAR 52.236-23, Responsibility of the Architect-Engineer Contractor, if another A-E were to represent or attempt to revise the current drawings and/or specifications. This clause states that the �Contractor shall be responsible for the professional quality, technical accuracy, and the coordination of all designs, drawings, specifications, and other services furnished by the Contractor�. However, if a new A-E were to make recommendations during the Type C services to revise or deviate from the original drawings or specifications, any liability resulting from those changes could not be attributed to the original A-E. This could potentially create a dangerous and complicated scenario if the Government needed to hold the responsible A-E party liable for any errors or deficiencies in the designs, drawings, and/or specifications. This action is being taken using the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.

title: Army Watercraft Systems Roundtable
description: SPECIAL NOTICE - U.S. Army Watercraft Systems Roundtable. The U.S. Army announces an Army Watercraft Systems Roundtable to be held on 2 December 2026, from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Central Standard Time (CST), at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, New Orleans, Louisiana for Prime shipbuilders, traditional and non-traditional commercial shipyards, industry, academia, and government stakeholders. HELP SHAPE THE FUTURE OF ARMY WATERCRAFT MODERNIZATION AND AUTONOMOUS VESSEL CAPABILITY: The U.S. Army seeks input from industry on the future of Army Watercraft systems, with emphasis on autonomous and optionally crewed vessel technologies. This roundtable will convene government stakeholders, prime shipbuilders, and commercial shipyards to discuss challenges, opportunities, and innovative approaches that support the Army Watercraft Modernization Strategy. The event will explore technologies and potential solutions that can help modernize, produce, sustain, and operate Army Watercraft in contested, distributed, and evolving operational environments. Discussions will focus on autonomous vessels, adaptable maritime systems, shipbuilding capacity, and industry innovation to advance future Army Watercraft capabilities. YOUR EXPERTISE SUPPORTS THE ARMY WATERCRAFT FUTURE: Insights from this roundtable and subsequent engagements will help inform Army consideration of future investments, acquisition approaches, modernization priorities, shipbuilding and sustainment capacity, and strategies for Army Watercraft systems. The U.S. Army also seeks industry perspectives on: barriers and challenges working with the U.S. Army, other Services, and the Department of War AND approaches to modernizing, overhauling, and sustaining the Army Watercraft fleet. Following the roundtable, participants may be invited to provide additional information regarding potential solutions to specific challenges and opportunities identified during the discussions. WHO SHOULD EXPRESS INTEREST: The Army is seeking participation from prime shipbuilders, traditional shipyards, and non-traditional commercial shipyards with relevant expertise in: Autonomous and optionally crewed vessel design, production, and integration / Watercraft design, construction, modernization, recapitalization, and sustainment / Maritime autonomy, navigation, sensing, and control systems / Hull design, modular construction, fabrication, and shipyard production capacity / Propulsion, power generation, energy storage, and hybrid systems / Command, control, communications, and mission-systems integration / Fleet readiness, maintenance, lifecycle support, and supply-chain resilience / Commercial maritime and inland-waterway technologies adaptable to Army requirements. PREPARE TO DISCUSS: Participants should be prepared to discuss mature capabilities, emerging technologies, production capacity, integration considerations, and potential approaches to supporting the Army Watercraft Modernization Strategy. AGENDA: 9:30 a.m. - 9:45 a.m. (Check-in and registration), 9:45 a.m. - 12:30 p.m. (Facilitated group sessions on autonomous vessel capabilities, modernization priorities, operational challenges, shipbuilding capacity, and industry perspectives), 12:30 p.m. - 1:00 p.m. (Break), 1:00 p.m. - 3:30 p.m. (Small-group and one-on-one sessions with Army representatives and participating shipbuilders and shipyards). title: U.S. Mission Burundi Local Guard Program
description: The Department of State is conducting market research to determine the degree of interest and capability by all business sizes (small and large) in providing local guard services at the U.S. Embassy Bujumbura, Burundi. The Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security plays an essential role in ensuring that foreign policy missions are accomplished in a safe and secure environment. The primary mission of the local guard service is to provide protection for United States personnel, facilities, and equipment from damage or loss due to violent attack and theft. The local guard services shall prevent unauthorized access; protect life; maintain order; deter criminal and terrorist attacks against employees, dependents, and property; and prevent damage to all U.S. assets. The NAICS code for these services is 561612. Responses must clearly demonstrate capabilities through examples of previous and/or current guard security contracts or experience closely related thereto. Vendors must specifically address the following capabilities: Current licenses, work authorizations in compliance with host country law required for the execution of work, including firearms permits and licenses. Licenses must be in the name of the U.S. business. Knowledge of and compliance with host country labor law which may require bonuses, specific minimum wage levels, premium pay for holidays, payments for social security, pensions, severance pay, sick or health benefits, childcare or any other benefit Knowledge of and compliance with host country tax law Ability to provide all types of insurance coverage required by host country in performance of services, such as automobile liability, comprehensive general liability, worker�s compensation, employer�s liability, etc. Furnishing, operating, and maintaining a radio network, including acquiring all licenses and permits that may be required for frequencies and the operation of all communications equipment Familiarity or experience with associated security equipment such as Guard Electronic Monitoring System (GEMS), Central Alarm Monitoring systems (CAMS), closed-circuit television systems, x-ray and explosive detection equipment Furnishing guard force equipment such as uniforms, vehicles, and weapons Ability to overcome language barriers Capability of instructing, providing, and qualifying personnel in the use of firearms, as well as x-ray equipment and radio equipment, including obtaining the access to a firearm training facility Ability to maintain a guard staff on a 24 hour 7 day a week basis with the ability to immediately backfill vacant positions due to resignations, rotations and illnesses due to a variety of reasons such as flu and food poisoning Capability of dealing with organized actions by direct labor personnel such as strikes (anticipated and unanticipated) and labor unrest (work slowdowns and/or organized failure of employees to report for shift changes) Ability to hire and train, including English language training and weapons training, if required, a guard staff consisting of host country nationals Ability to provide trained equipment technicians for all vehicles, radios and weapons required in the performance of the contract Ability to train a sizeable workforce to adapt quickly to unfamiliar laws and customs as well as the ability of company officials to gain quickly information regarding the laws and customs needed to maintain and equip such a workforce Experience or capability of getting contractor-furnished equipment and goods through customs and/or similar governmental agencies of the host country Understanding import and export regulations Understanding and familiarity of the Arms Export Control Act (AECA) and International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR) and the capability of complying with both by the performance date of any contract awarded requiring the execution of this Statute (22 U.S.C. 2778-2780) Managing smooth contract transition efforts. Ability to safely keep and track Government-Furnished Property Ability to screen personnel to meet suitability requirements for guard force positions Strong skill in instant, situational decision-making, e.g., response to threats Organized billing and invoicing procedures It is requested that all interested parties submit their capabilities by e-mail to Brian Averhart at AverhartB@state.gov addressing each of the above requirements by 12:00 EST, 27 November 2026. Interested parties shall also complete the attached Contractor Information Sheet. If you have any questions or comments, please reference this Sources Sought Notice when emailing. At this time, the U.S. Department of State does not guarantee that any future contracts may be awarded covering the aforementioned duties and responses to this Sources Sought notice do not bind the U.S. Department of State to any agreement with the responder, be it explicit or implied.

description: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Financial Services Center (FSC) Workforce Assessment Services Request for Information (RFI) Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. title: Notice of Intent - Illumina MiSeq i100 series instruments
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Illumina, Inc. Acquisition Description: The purpose of this acquisition is to purchase two Illumina MiSeq i100 series instruments. These instruments will be used by the NIH HLA Laboratory to produce high resolution HLA typing results for the numerous transplant protocols supported by the laboratory. It will replace the current Illumina MiSeq instruments in the lab that were purchased in 2021 and 2022. The vendor will discontinue service on the current model of the MiSeq. New instruments are required to ensure time to validate these replacements before discontinuation of service. The total dollar value for this order is $139,100.52. The MiSeq is an integrated instrument that performs clonal amplification, genomic DNA sequencing, and data analysis with base calling, alignment, variant calling, and reporting in a single run. The MiSeq provides the Lab with the highest HLA typing results possible. The transplant protocols served by the HLA Lab require highest resolution possible to increase the chance of a successful transplant. The HLA Lab currently owns two MiSeq instruments, so the procedures and Quality Control assessments are in place. The order aims to replace the Illumina Miseq � s/n M07700 (property ID is 02223449) and s/n M08636 (property ID is 02268689) that were purchased in 2019 and 2022. Replacement is necessary to ensure proper performance of these instruments prior to discontinuation of service for the current model of the Illumina MiSeq instruments by the vendor. The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 253(c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. All responsible sources that could provide the required may submit a capability statement that will be considered by email (subject line to reference NOI-OLAO-CC-27-000836) by 12:00 PM eastern standard time on 11/27/2026 to: valerie.gregorio@nih.gov. All responses received by the closing date of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
description: GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. General: Construction project is to be completed within 120 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards. Safety submittals shall be completed and approved prior to the commencement of on-site construction work. Material selection submittals shall be completed and approved prior to ordering of materials for the project. The building tenants not in the construction areas will remain at work in the buildings during this construction. Patients will remain on the floor in areas not under construction, so the contractor shall make patient safety, and infection control measures a priority. The contractor shall coordinate work locations and schedules with VA COR to minimize impact to building tenants. All electrical, carpentry, architectural, mechanical work, product design, project management, and other work needed on this project shall be provided by the Contractor. All required electrical work, low, medium, or high voltage, shall be installed and terminated by the Contractor. No wiring or cabling shall be abandoned in place. All piping, cabling, and wiring shall be labeled. All cabling and patch cabling shall match the VAMC s station-standard colors. The installation must, at a minimum, be in accordance with all applicable codes indicated in the Department of Veterans Affairs Design Manuals and VA .PUBLICATIONS (Master Construction Specifications, Construction Standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Underwriters Laboratory (UL), International Building Code IBC 2003, and National Electric Code (NEC) building codes and standards and the VA Information Security Handbook 6500.6, 6550.0 etc.). The Contractor shall read and be familiar with the most current editions of the applicable codes, standards, guides, and manuals. Sources can be accessed at the Office of Construction and Facilities Management s Technical Information Library (TIL) (http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL). Any penetrations through any floors, ceilings, or walls shall be fire caulked, or otherwise fire sealed, and shall be done in this contract to meet VA standards and NFPA standards. Contractor shall utilize the VAMC s station-standard fire stop products or approved equal product(s). The station-standard products are SpecSeal fire caulk product is SpecSeal SSS Intumescent Firestop Sealant; and, if needed, the SpecSeal Composite Sheet may be used in areas approved by the COR. The Contractor shall inquire of the COR if any existing equipment, fixtures, hardware, doors, frames, or any other property removed is desired to be retained by the VA for reuse elsewhere within the medical center, at the time of removal. If the VA desires to retain an item, the Contractor shall deliver it to a location designated by the COR. If the VA does not desire to retain an item, the Contractor shall dispose of it properly off-station. The new components installed shall be tested and commissioned, re-certified, and/or tested before VA acceptance. All testing parameters shall be provided by the Contractor with source references to the COR and 3rd-party reviewer before testing begins. Copies of all test reports must be provided to the COR. HVAC systems that have changes made to them as part of this project, beyond diffuser replacement, shall be tested and balanced by the Contractor. Any IT data cables installed or modified as part of this effort shall be tested after installation. Test methods and plans shall be coordinated with the COR. Any Med Gas systems modified as part of this effort shall be re-certified back to the closest shut-off in the system. The Contractor shall arrange for any required re-certification as part of this contract and shall provide plans and results to the COR for approval. Fire alarm devices that are tied into the building fire alarm system, that are replaced or relocated as a result of this work, shall be tested before that phase of the project is complete. The Contractor shall arrange for all required fire alarm testing. If a building s fire alarm system is under warranty, testing must be accomplished by the contractor who holds the warranty. description: Effective Date: 01/15/2026 Revision: 03 Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 This solicitation is unrestricted, Full and Open competition. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 325413 with a small business size standard of 1250 employees. The FSC/PSC is 6550. The Network Contracting Office 5 is seeking to purchase BD FACSLyric Flow Cytometry Reagents/Supplies for the Baltimore VAMC located at 10 N Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: See Attachment labeled Line Item Template Note: All quantities are estimates Statement of Work BD FACSLyric Flow Cytometry Reagents/Supplies Introduction: Technology: Flow cytometry is a technology that simultaneously measures and then analyzes multiple physical characteristics of single particles, usually cells, as they flow in a fluid stream through a beam of light. The parameters measured include the particle size, granularity or internal complexity, and fluorescence intensity. An optical-to-electronic coupling system determines these characteristics by recording how the cell or particle scatters incident laser light and emits fluorescence. These scatter and fluorescence signals, detected by the instrument, provide information about the cell s size, internal complexity, and relative fluorescence intensity. BD Multisets reagents employ fluorescence triggering, allowing direct fluorescence gating of the lymphocyte population to reduce contamination of lyse-resistant or nucleated red blood cells in the gate. To prepare for flow analysis, a patient s whole blood is added to the reagent, and the fluorochrome-labeled antibodies in the reagent bind specifically to the leucocyte s surface antigens. During acquisition, the stained cells travel past the laser beam and scatter the laser light. The staining pattern of each population, combined with forward-scattered light (FSC) and side-scattered light (SSC) data, can be used to identify which cell populations are present in the patient sample. Photodetectors (Photo iodide & Photomultiplier tubes/PMT) convert the light signals to electronic signals, which are then converted into digital channel numbers for display on a data plot. Scope of work: General: The offeror shall provide to the Veterans Affairs Medical Health Care System at Baltimore VAMC all reagents and supplies for flow cytometry testing in the Hematology section of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service. The reagents/supplies will be used for CD4/CD8 count testing and the phenotyping of white blood cells in the leukemia and lymphoma assay using the FACSLyric. QC material and calibration material are used for the detection of voltages and spectral overlap to monitor optimal cytometer settings, checks, and track the daily performance. Term of Agreement: The contract term is for 1 year. Performance Period: 12/03/2026 to 12/02/2027 Reagents: Monoclonal Antibodies for Leukemia and lymphoma diagnostic. The quantity of reagents in this list was based on the data collected from the volume of patients received in 2024 and 2025. The leukemia population was around 300 patients, and the CD4/CD8 T-cell helper testing request was around 3000 patients Place of Performance/Place of Delivery Address: 10 N Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201.
